clue.text: Limp little books found in dingy place

indicators.note: things found in a place sit inside it, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: a hole is a dingy, poky place to live
B is the short form of book, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A sickly stack of tiny volumes turns up in some grubby den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limp' looks like an adjective for the books, but it is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobble is to walk awkwardly with an injured leg, a synonym of limp as a verb.

clue.text: Maiden, perhaps, says it's your turn to speak

definitions.text: says it's your turn to speak

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket a maiden is one kind of set of six balls bowled

blocks.clueFragment: says it's your turn to speak
blocks.note: second meaning: the radio word meaning I've finished, go ahead

explanation.surface: A shy young woman tells you politely that you may now talk.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one in which no runs are scored, so 'Maiden, perhaps' gives an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket overs include maidens, and radio operators finish each message with this word to hand the channel across.

clue.text: A fuel tub I mended is not ugly

indicators.note: something mended has been put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has repaired an old fuel container and admires how it looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely to look at is the opposite of hideous, so the understated phrase works as a litotes for good looks.

clue.text: Absolute savage in tree

indicators.note: to savage something is to maul it, so the letters that follow are torn about

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A total wild man is living up in the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolute savage' reads as noun phrase, but savage is a verb working on the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and complete are synonyms, as in absolute or whole control without any limit.

clue.text: Contrite writer, one seen in front of canvas dwelling

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Roman numeral for one
a tent is a home made of canvas

explanation.surface: A repentant author is spotted outside a camping shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sorry for wrongdoing and wishing to make amends is remorseful, the same sense as contrite.

clue.text: True street guide - you don't know him from Adam

definitions.text: you don't know him from Adam

blocks.note: true in the sense of exact and flawless, as a true circle
the usual abbreviation for street
Rangers were the senior section of the Girl Guides

explanation.surface: A trustworthy guide to the streets turns out to be someone you've never met.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Guide movement's older members were called Rangers, so a ranger is a kind of guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Not knowing someone from Adam means having no idea who they are, which describes a complete unknown.

clue.text: Number: a thousand in a gathering as a rule

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, so it goes inside

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
a rally is a mass gathering
the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A count of a thousand people at a meeting is typical.
explanation.walkthrough: The thousand goes in just after the first letter of the gathering, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually and generally are synonyms of the adverb meaning as is ordinarily the case.

clue.text: Settle up for a clocklike device

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: to remit a sum is to pay or settle it

explanation.surface: Paying the bill in exchange for a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle up' looks like one phrase for paying, but up is the separate instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen or egg timer measures intervals and rings, working much as a small clock does.

clue.text: Remarkable school put up with a local celebrity

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means written upwards, from the bottom

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school
a local worthy is a person of standing in a community

explanation.surface: A striking school agreed to host a well-known local figure.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON reversed gives NOTE. A worthy is an old-fashioned word for an important person in a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of note deserves attention, so it is remarkable or significant.

clue.text: Bottle or tin kept in check

indicators.note: something kept in another thing is held inside it

blocks.note: to deter is to check or hold back
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Should the drink go in glass or a tin held under control?
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a stoppered glass vessel for serving wine, a kind of fancy bottle.

clue.text: Turned to me to get into religious eduction, though far away

indicators.note: turned round means the words that follow are read backwards
getting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
RE is the school subject Religious Education (the clue's 'eduction' is a misprint)

explanation.surface: Someone converted to faith through religious classes, yet seems distant.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education; the clue's 'eduction' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote describes a place or person distant in space or feeling, a direct synonym.

clue.text: This for a honeymoon, but the record was faulty

indicators.note: a faulty item has gone wrong, so the letters before come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it is fodder as well as part of the signal

explanation.surface: Newlyweds' trip spoiled because the music player broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a honeymoon is for two people, and the saying describes an unwanted third.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a third person spoils things for a couple, which is exactly the situation on a honeymoon.

clue.text: Wave to attract pale animal

blocks.note: first meaning: a foam-crested wave breaking at sea
second meaning: a light-coloured steed, taken literally

explanation.surface: Waving your hand to lure a pale creature over.
explanation.walkthrough: White horses are the foamy crests on waves in a choppy sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call breaking foam crests on the sea by this name, and literally it is a light-coated mount.

clue.text: Cooker turns iron hot and cold

indicators.note: turning round means the following pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
H for hot, as on a tap
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A stove flips an iron between hot and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooker' looks like the stove, but here it is a person who cooks; FE H C reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who prepares food in a restaurant kitchen is one who cooks, hence a cooker.

clue.text: Mere talk describes this turn in skiing

indicators.note: to describe a curve is to trace it out, so the letters are traced into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Just chatting is how someone explains a manoeuvre on the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: The telemark is a Norwegian skiing technique and turn performed with one knee bent low.

clue.text: Delivery boy holding pickle, green as it might be

indicators.note: something only as it might be is not in its settled form, so the letters can be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: to be in a pickle is to be in a mess
taken as written

explanation.surface: An inexperienced lad carrying a jar of chutney makes deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier who carries messages or parcels is the classic job for an errand lad.

clue.text: Friend with moving meter provides symbol of success

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift their places

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mate with an emotionally stirring gauge gives a sign of triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Palm leaves were the ancient prize of victors, hence bearing the palm means winning.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm branch has long been an emblem of victory, and the plant itself stands for that triumph.

clue.text: A good man, a lieutenant, holding combat to be courageous

indicators.note: a thing holding something has it inside

blocks.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good man
taken as written
the standard abbreviation of lieutenant
war is armed combat

explanation.surface: A decent soldier and a junior officer in battle show bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: ST and A, then LT holding WAR gives L-WAR-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means loyal, sturdy and brave, close in sense to valiant or bold.

clue.text: Thus half one's home is in this part of London

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, so the rest is dropped

blocks.note: so means thus, in this way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says part of their house lies in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of HOME is HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of central London's West End known for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: I'm like a stalactite in dark red volcanic rock

indicators.note: a stalactite hangs from the roof, upside down, so the word is turned over
one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
puce is a dark purplish red

explanation.surface: A rock speaks, comparing itself to a cave formation in a crimson setting.
explanation.walkthrough: A stalactite hangs from a cave roof, so in a down entry it suggests letters turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light porous stone formed from frothy lava, a classic igneous rock.

clue.text: Summary law gives less than the correct amount

blocks.note: a summary is a short version
a measure is a legislative act or law

explanation.surface: A swiftly passed statute leaves people shortchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: Summary here sounds like summary justice, but it gives a shortened word for brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving short measure means selling customers a smaller quantity than they paid for.

clue.text: Hurried to get account in the red

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written; being in the red means in debt
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Rushed to open a bank account while overdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced is the past tense of race, meaning moved quickly or rushed, matching hurried.

clue.text: Blue Western concealed by university teacher

indicators.note: something concealed by another is hidden inside it

blocks.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: A sad cowboy film is being hidden by a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' and 'Western' look like a film genre pair, but blue is the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue and feeling down are both idioms for sad and low-spirited.

clue.text: Good backlog not finished for tradesman

indicators.note: not finished means the word stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the surface word split in two: back is the turning signal, and a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A merchant has a fine pile of unfinished orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backlog' is one word on the surface, split here into back and log.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food and household goods, a kind of tradesman.

clue.text: Morally suspect behaviour of departing boy

blocks.note: going means leaving
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad leaving home has been up to no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on is a disapproving word for dubious or scandalous activities happening somewhere.

clue.text: Bonnet, perhaps, hides top set of wheels

blocks.note: the head is the top of something
a gear is a set of toothed wheels

explanation.surface: A car's bonnet covers the gearwheels in the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonnet' and 'wheels' suggest a car; a bonnet is also a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is one example of a hat, and hats in general are coverings worn on the head.

clue.text: Short journey made for another in Clermont-Ferrand

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the place name that follows

blocks.note: the last six letters of the French city's name

explanation.surface: A trip on someone's behalf to a city in central France.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a small trip to deliver or collect something on behalf of somebody else.
